title: Inventory Management Specialist (Cpl to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
5.     MOS 3051, Inventory Management Specialist (Cpl to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. Inventory Management Specialists perform various duties
within logistics chain management to include receiving, inspecting, locating,
storing, rotating (first in-first out), safekeeping, issuing, preparing,
shipping, material return, and disposal of materiel and equipment. These
clerks maintain automated or manual locator systems in order to conduct
inventories, maintain records of issued durable goods, and monitor shelf-life
items, separate and handle hazardous material according to its classification
and as indicated by material safety data sheets, input data entry
transactions, and retrieval of historical records. They utilize and maintain
handheld optical character recognition scanners, devices, and multimedia



                                         3-267                        Enclosure (1)
 3125                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



retrieval systems. These Marines are licensed to operate material handling
equipment (MHE) in both garrison and deployed environments as well as operate
bulk and small parts conveyer systems used in automated warehousing
operations. Marines assigned to this occupational field receive, sort,
document, and store inventory as well as prepare, pack, and issue inventory
in open, enclosed, and hazardous material storage areas. They will use
detailed technical data for the development and execution of a care and
storage requirements to include the development of storage space
requirements, per weight, cube, and clearance factors by categories of
supply.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess a CL score of 95 or higher.

            (2) Security requirement:   requires favorably adjudicated NACLC.

        (3) Must have a valid civilian motor vehicle operator's license in
order to be assigned the 3051 MOS.

        (4) No convictions by court-martial, civilian courts, or non-judicial
punishment of any act involving larceny or theft.

        (5) In accordance with MANMED Chapter 15, Section 107:       the following
medical requirements must be met:

            (a) Has distant visual acuity of at least 20/40 with or without
corrective lenses.

            (b) First perceives a forced whisper in the better ear at not
less than 5 feet with or without the use of hearing aid.

                (c) Has no impairment of:

                    1.   A hand or finger which interferes with prehension or
power grasping.

                2. An arm, foot, or leg limitation which interferes with the
ability to perform normal task associated with operating CMV (or equivalent).

    c. Requirements. Complete the Inventory Management Basic Course
(M03SCM1) at the MCSSS, Camp Lejeune, NC.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (r), Supply Chain and Materiel Management Training and Readiness
Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Inventory Clerk 222.387.026.

            (2) Data entry Clerk 203.582.054.

            (3) Warehouse Supervisors 929.137-022.

            (4) Stock Clerks and Order Fillers 43-5081.

            (5) Shipping, Receiving, and Traffic Clerks 43-5071.



                                         3-268                        Enclosure (1)
 3125                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L



        (6) Entry level Marines (Cpl to Pvt) holding entry level ranks
perform the duties and tasks comparable to the following classifications:

               (a) Warehouse Clerk 43-5081.

               (b) Stock Clerks and Order Fillers 43-5081.

               (c) Shipping, Receiving, and Traffic Clerks 43-5071.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.




                                         3-269                        Enclosure (1)
 3126                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: The Supply Chain Materiel Management OccFld includes personnel in the areas of ground supply chain management operations, inventory management, preservation and packaging, hazardous materials storage and handling operations, fiscal accounting and purchasing, and contracting procedures pursuant to the Federal Acquisition Regulations. Duties involve administrative procedures, familiarization with state, federal, and Department of Defense regulations, and the use of material handling equipment in the movement and storage of materiel and equipment. In all MOSs within the OccFld, technical skills are required regarding military and commercial specifications on materiel and equipment being procured, stored, and maintained. These skills and duties must be performed in garrison, afloat, expeditionary, and combat environments. These Marines are required to have an operational understanding in executing supply chain functions and programs, some of which are unique to the service and Department of Defense as well as provide for effective and efficient end-to-end materiel support in the area of materiel management. Marines assigned to the occupational field are trained to utilize data scanning, and retrieval devices, office and inventory management procedures, automated information data entry and external systems interface procedures, asset accounting functions, financial budget formulation, management and analysis, and the proper handling, storage, and disposal of hazardous material. Formal schooling is provided to Marines entering the OccFld. Types of entry-level billets such as automated information services supply stock control clerk (retail and intermediate), inventory clerk, shipping/receiving clerk, packaging specialist, fiscal/ budget clerk, contract specialist and automated information systems user.

The Supply Chain Materiel Management OccFld includes personnel in the areas of ground supply chain management operations, inventory management, preservation and packaging, hazardous materials storage and handling operations, fiscal accounting and purchasing, and contracting procedures pursuant to the Federal Acquisition Regulations.
Perform administrative duties, such as serving as department heads.

Duties involve administrative procedures, familiarization with state, federal, and Department of Defense regulations, and the use of material handling equipment in the movement and storage of materiel and equipment.
Manage activities related to strategic or tactical purchasing, material requirements planning, controlling inventory, warehousing, or receiving.

These Marines are required to have an operational understanding in executing supply chain functions and programs, some of which are unique to the service and Department of Defense as well as provide for effective and efficient end-to-end materiel support in the area of materiel management.
Provide training on hazardous material or waste cleanup procedures and technologies.

Marines assigned to the occupational field are trained to utilize data scanning, and retrieval devices, office and inventory management procedures, automated information data entry and external systems interface procedures, asset accounting functions, financial budget formulation, management and analysis, and the proper handling, storage, and disposal of hazardous material.
Operate typing, adding, calculating, or billing machines.

Types of entry-level billets such as automated information services supply stock control clerk (retail and intermediate), inventory clerk, shipping/receiving clerk, packaging specialist, fiscal/ budget clerk, contract specialist and automated information systems user.
Maintain inventory, ordering materials as required.

Inventory Management Specialists perform various duties within logistics chain management to include receiving, inspecting, locating, storing, rotating (first in-first out), safekeeping, issuing, preparing, shipping, material return, and disposal of materiel and equipment.
Operate various types of equipment, such as computer scanning equipment, addressographs, mimeographs, optical character readers, and bar-code sorters.
They utilize and maintain handheld optical character recognition scanners, devices, and multimedia retrieval systems.
Operate ship loading and unloading equipment, conveyors, hoists, and other specialized material handling equipment such as railroad tank car unloading equipment.

These Marines are licensed to operate material handling equipment (MHE) in both garrison and deployed environments as well as operate bulk and small parts conveyer systems used in automated warehousing operations.
Order supplies or equipment and issue them to personnel.
Marines assigned to this occupational field receive, sort, document, and store inventory as well as prepare, pack, and issue inventory in open, enclosed, and hazardous material storage areas.
Identify required data, data acquisition plans, and test parameters, setting up equipment to conform to these specifications.

They will use detailed technical data for the development and execution of a care and storage requirements to include the development of storage space requirements, per weight, cube, and clearance factors by categories of supply.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
